newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: NATO's Solana says seeks closer ties with Moldova.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana says seeks closer ties with Moldova.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, on his first visit to the Moldovan capital Chisinau, said on Monday he hoped for closer ties with the former Soviet republic.

"We are facing important decisions on the security of Europe in 1997, and I would like to exchange views with the authorities of Moldova on these," Solana told reporters at the airport. "I would like to increase bilateral ties between NATO and Moldova."
Solana's one-day visit to Moldova is part of a longer trip to former Soviet republics cooperating with NATO within the framework of the alliance's Partnership for Peace programme.
Moldova signed up for Partnership for Peace in March 1994 and its soldiers have already participated in 15 NATO exercises.
Moldova, sandwiched between Romania and Ukraine, says it has no intention of joining any military bloc, either within the Commonwealth of Independent States, or in the West.
The constitution says Moldova is neutral and does not allow the stationing of foreign troops on its territory.

However, 6,000 Russian troops are based in the separatist Dnestr region bordering Ukraine. Separatist leaders declared Dnestr independent in 1990, but no other country has recognised the sliver of industrial land as an independent state.
